Thomson, M.J., Evenson, E.J., Kempe, M.J. and Goodfellow, H.D. (2000). Control of greenhouse gas emissions from electric arc furnace steelmaking: evaluation methodology with case studies. Ironmaking and Steelmaking, 27(4), 273-279. No DOI printed.

Locators are printed page numbers (273-279; PDF page = printed - 272). Life-cycle GHG model of an EAF melt shop with two case studies: a Canadian conventional EAF (case 1) and a UK shaft scrap-preheating EAF (case 2). The paper prints no absolute electricity use per tonne, only changes, so the main file holds only the direct emission components (emissions-process = net charge carbon plus injected graphite; emissions-combustion = natural gas burners) for baseline cases 1A and 2A (Tables 6 and 8) and optimised cases 1C and 2C (Table 9, UK grid). Table 9 values are rounded to integers. Life-cycle totals incl. electricity and lime are in other-values. Measures file: Table 1 (Worrell et al. 1994 US data, reprinted: electricity saving, retrofit capital cost, operating cost change) and the four case-study improvements. Trap: Table 9 column "Other" lumps other carbon and other indirect; emissions-process excludes the "other carbon sources" line (6.2-9.2 kg/t). Retrofit costs are US dollars of 1994 (printed "all data are for US furnaces in 1994").
